title: An Inspector Calls
description: 50 Flashcards covering J.B. Priestley's An Inspector Calls (Plot, Characters, Themes, Quotes).

cards.q: Who wrote An Inspector Calls?
cards.a: J.B. Priestley

cards.q: In what year is the play set?
In what year was the play written and first performed?
cards.a: 1945 (first performed in USSR), 1946 (in UK)

cards.q: How does the play's setting (1912) contrast with its writing time (1945)?
cards.a: 1912 was pre-WW1 (Edwardian era class system), 1945 was post-WW2 (desire for a fairer, socialist society).

cards.q: Which affluent manufacturing town is the play set in?
cards.a: Brumley (a fictional Midlands town)

cards.q: What is Arthur Birling's primary concern in life?
cards.a: Business, profit, and maintaining his social status.

cards.q: Quote Arthur Birling: 'A man has to make his own way—has to look after himself—and ______'
cards.a: his family too, of course

cards.q: Which historical event does Mr Birling say is 'impossible'?
cards.a: War (The First World War)

cards.q: What does Mr Birling call the Titanic?
cards.a: 'Unsinkable, absolutely unsinkable'

cards.q: What dramatic device is used when Birling talks about the Titanic and war?
cards.a: Dramatic Irony

cards.q: Who is Sybil Birling?
cards.a: Arthur's wife, a cold woman and her husband's social superior.

cards.q: Why is Arthur Birling trying to impress Gerald Croft?
cards.a: Gerald's family (Crofts Limited) is socially and economically superior to the Birlings.

cards.q: What is the name of the girl who died?
cards.a: Eva Smith (also known as Daisy Renton)

cards.q: How did Eva Smith die?
cards.a: She drank strong disinfectant (suicide).

cards.q: What was the Inspector's name?
cards.a: Inspector Goole

cards.q: How is the Inspector's lighting described when he enters?
cards.a: The lighting changes from 'pink and intimate' to 'brighter and harder'.

cards.q: Why did Arthur Birling sack Eva Smith?
cards.a: She was one of the ringleaders of a strike asking for a pay rise (from 22.5 to 25 shillings a week).

cards.q: How did Sheila Birling get Eva Smith sacked from Milwards?
cards.a: She complained out of jealousy because Eva looked better in a dress than she did.

cards.q: How does Sheila feel after finding out her role in Eva's death?
cards.a: Guilty, repentant, and distressed.

cards.q: Where did Gerald Croft meet Daisy Renton (Eva Smith)?
cards.a: The Palace Bar

cards.q: What did Gerald Croft do for Daisy Renton?
cards.a: He rescued her from Alderman Meggarty, gave her money, and let her stay in some rooms he had the keys to. They had an affair.

cards.q: How does Sybil Birling know Eva Smith?
cards.a: Eva came to her Women's Charity Organization asking for help when she was pregnant.

cards.q: Why did Sybil Birling refuse to help Eva?
cards.a: Eva initially used the name 'Mrs Birling', which offended Sybil, calling it an piece of 'gross impertinence'.

cards.q: Who does Sybil Birling blame for Eva's death?
cards.a: The father of her unborn child.

cards.q: Who was the father of Eva's baby?
cards.a: Eric Birling

cards.q: How did Eric meet Eva/Daisy?
cards.a: In the Palace Bar. He was drunk and forced his way into her lodgings.

cards.q: How did Eric get the money he gave to Eva?
cards.a: He stole it from his father's company office.

cards.q: What is the Inspector's final message about humanity?
cards.a: 'We don't live alone. We are members of one body. We are responsible for each other.'

cards.q: What does the Inspector warn will happen if men do not learn their lesson?
cards.a: They will be taught it in 'fire and blood and anguish'.

cards.q: How does Priestley use the Inspector?
cards.a: As his mouthpiece to express his socialist views.

cards.q: What happens after the Inspector leaves?
cards.a: Gerald returns and reveals that 'Inspector Goole' is not a real police officer.

cards.q: How do the older generation (Arthur and Sybil) react to the revelation that the Inspector was fake?
cards.a: They are relieved and think they are off the hook, reverting to their old ways.

cards.q: How do the younger generation (Sheila and Eric) react?
cards.a: They believe that whether the Inspector was real or not, the guilt remains the same.

cards.q: What twist happens at the very end of the play?
cards.a: The phone rings: a girl has just died on her way to the infirmary after swallowing disinfectant, and a police inspector is on his way.

cards.q: Quote Inspector Goole: 'There are millions and millions and millions of ______'
cards.a: Eva Smiths and John Smiths still left with us

cards.q: Quote Sheila Birling: 'But these girls aren't cheap labour - they're ______'
cards.a: people

cards.q: Quote Mrs Birling: 'Girls of that ______'
cards.a: class

cards.q: What does Eric represent regarding the younger generation?
cards.a: The capacity for change and accepting responsibility.

cards.q: What theme is highlighted by the Birlings' initial dinner party?
cards.a: Capitalist greed, complacency, and the illusion of a perfect middle-class family.

cards.q: What does the play suggest about social class?
cards.a: It criticizes the rigid class system of 1912 and shows how the upper classes abuse their power over the working classes.

cards.q: What role does Edna the maid play?
cards.a: She highlights the invisible working-class presence in the Birling household and announces the Inspector's arrival.

cards.q: What is Priestley's views on capitalism as depicted in the play?
cards.a: He criticizes capitalism as selfish and exploitative, advocating for socialism instead.

cards.q: What is the significance of the photograph the Inspector shows?
cards.a: He only shows it to one person at a time, allowing for the possibility that they are all recognizing different girls.

cards.q: How does the play follow the 'Aristotelian Unities'?
cards.a: It takes place in one location, continuously in real-time, focusing on one single plot.

cards.q: What genres could 'An Inspector Calls' be classified as?
cards.a: A morality play, a well-made play, and a whodunit/detective thriller.

cards.q: Who says: 'You're beginning to pretend now that nothing's really happened at all.'
cards.a: Eric Birling

cards.q: Who says: 'Everything's all right now, Sheila. What about this ring?'
cards.a: Gerald Croft

cards.q: What does the disinfectant symbolize?
cards.a: The harsh reality and suffering of the working classes; purging/cleansing the Birlings of their secrets.

cards.q: Why is the play called cyclical or having a circular structure?
cards.a: It ends exactly as it threatens to begin again: a police inspector arriving to investigate a suicide.

cards.q: What does Gerald's character demonstrate about the young upper class?
cards.a: He is younger but holds older, traditional views; representing that the aristocracy's attitudes are entrenched.
